lines.text: Everyone knows you should never put metal in a microwave, but do you know why it sparks?
Microwaves heat food by blasting electromagnetic radiation that makes water molecules vibrate wildly.
Thick metal walls reflect these waves harmlessly, which is why the microwave oven itself is made of steel.
However, thin metals like aluminum foil or fork prongs have billions of free electrons.
The intense electric waves push these electrons into sharp corners, building massive electrical voltage.
When the voltage gets high enough, it rips through the air, creating explosive fiery plasma arcs.
So never put wrinkled foil or utensils in your microwave unless you want fireworks!
